about.units: Angles in degrees, offsets in pixels on the 320x320 frame (origin top-left, y down).
about.rotation: rot.<part> rotates that part about its rig.json pivot. Positive = clockwise on screen. Children inherit their parent's transform (rig.json parents: torso carries head, arms and scarf; arm-front carries tool; legs and torso hang from root).
about.side view (facing right): Arms and legs hang down at 0. NEGATIVE swings a limb FORWARD (toward +x, the facing direction): -90 = pointing straight ahead, -180 = straight up. Positive swings it back. Torso: POSITIVE leans forward. Scarf: positive trails it back.
about.front and back views: arm-left (image left) goes out and up with POSITIVE angles (150 = up in a V); arm-right goes out and up with NEGATIVE angles. Same for the legs.
about.tool: rot.tool is the prop's extra rotation about the grip (172,238), on top of arm-front's. Neutral prop: handle straight up from the grip, working end forward. The prop file is <root>/props/<prop>.png; 'prop' may be set per animation or per frame.
about.offsets: torso_dy moves the torso (and so head, arms, scarf, tool) up/down. move.<part> = [dx,dy] moves one part (and its children). root_dx/root_dy (alias dx/dy) shift the whole finished frame by whole pixels, so they never blur.
about.head: 'head' or 'head-blink' per frame.
about.layers: Optional per-animation layer order (back to front) replacing rig.json's; carry draws the sack behind the head.
about.props: pickaxe and hammer: handle up from the grip, head at the top. coal-sack: grip at the knot, the sack body hanging BELOW the knot (carry's tool angle assumes that).
about.ground_lock: When true, each frame is shifted vertically so the lowest leg pixel sits on ground_y (304) before root_dy is applied. This keeps feet planted while legs swing; a jump is root_dy < 0 (the checker allows exactly that).
about.pose animations: An animation with 'pose' uses the painted image characters/<name>/poses/<pose>.png instead of the rig. Per frame: dx, dy (whole pixels), sx, sy (scale about (centre_x, ground_y), so the body stays on the ground), pose_frame (cell of a multi-frame pose).
